requirement_text.REQ-124: MOB-2 (docs/mobile/requirements.md) needs GET /tenant-config to return { realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind } WITHOUT a bearer token: the mobile app calls it to discover which realm to authenticate against, so by definition it has no token yet. Verified against lib/ on 2026-08-21, this is two gaps, not one: (a) Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig is a stub whose routes land in REQ-078; and (b) Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline mounts it behind Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, so implementing the route is not sufficient -- it would still demand the token the caller cannot have. Resolve (b) explicitly: either an unauthenticated variant mounted ahead of AuthPipeline, or a documented exemption inside it. Pick one and record why in the moduledoc. This is the gate for the entire mobile tier -- without it the app cannot reach a login screen -- which is why it is sequenced first in docs/mobile/build-order.md phase M-0. Security scope: an unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data is a tenant-data path by definition and needs SECURITY-REVIEWER. The response must expose only what bootstrap requires. Check the shape field-by-field against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md -- in particular whether an unauthenticated caller enumerating slugs can learn which tenants exist, and what the answer should be for a slug that does not exist.

task.description: Run the standard REVIEWER procedure (.claude/agents/reviewer.md) against git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex lib/letflow/router.ex. This adds a second, near-duplicate router module (Letflow.Routers.MobileTenantConfig) alongside the existing Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig -- the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req124-mobile-tenant-config.md §1) argues explicitly for two separate modules over a shared/parameterized one, with stated tradeoffs (isolated INV-2 allowlists, avoids one function auditing two response contracts, matches the project's one-module-per-concern router pattern). Give this decision genuine scrutiny rather than treating it as pre-settled by the design gate -- is duplicating the never-error/anti-oracle reasoning across two moduledocs and two safe_get_tenant_by_slug/1-shaped functions the CORRECT amount of duplication here, or does it cross into a crutch/copy-paste smell docs/anti-patterns.md would flag? Also check: idiomatic Plug.Router usage, no supervision-tree involvement (this is stateless request handling, not a supervised process, so that check is expected N/A -- confirm it, don't skip it), and consistency with the router-decomposition precedent set by REQ-070/REQ-078 (one small single-purpose router module per concern, forwarded from Letflow.Router).
acceptance_criteria: Idiomatic vs. crutch verdict on the new module, with reasoning
Supervision integrity check explicitly stated as N/A with why (stateless Plug.Router, not a supervised process)
Scope-creep check: nothing touched beyond what REQ-124 required
Decision-record consistency: mount pattern matches REQ-078's established precedent, no unauthorized divergence
Explicit verdict on the two-module-vs-one duplication tradeoff named in task.description -- accept, or flag as a genuine crutch with a specific alternative

result.summary: Idiomatic vs. crutch: Letflow.Routers.MobileTenantConfig is a clean, idiomatic Plug.Router sub-router -- plug(:match)/plug(:dispatch), a single GET '/' handler, a catch-all match _ -> Response.not_found/1, hand-built response map, no macro/behaviour machinery. No GenServer standing in for a state machine, no crutch in that sense. Supervision integrity: N/A, correctly -- this is stateless per-request Plug dispatch under Bandit/the existing HTTP acceptor pool, not a supervised long-lived process, so Letflow.InstanceSupervisor and process-per-instance isolation are not implicated at all; nothing here collapses any existing isolation boundary. Scope creep: none -- diff is exactly one new single-purpose router module plus one forward/2 line in Letflow.Router, both scoped tightly to REQ-124; no new abstraction, behaviour, or generic plumbing introduced. Decision-record consistency: mount placement (forwarded from Letflow.Router, declared after /api/tenant-config and before the /api/v1 forward, so it never enters Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline) exactly mirrors REQ-078's Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig precedent; Letflow.Plugs.Cors coverage is origin-based so it applies with no change needed, matching the existing module. No divergence from any docs/migration/decisions/ record. Two-module-vs-one verdict: ACCEPT the split itself -- config_map/1 vs mobile_config_map/1 are genuinely different INV-2 allowlists (2-key vs 5-key) built for different callers, matches the project's established one-module-per-concern router pattern (10 existing single-purpose Letflow.Routers.* modules), and keeping them in separate functions/modules is the correct call for auditability, per the design's own §1 reasoning. HOWEVER: safe_get_tenant_by_slug/1 in mobile_tenant_config.ex (lines 186-196) is byte-for-byte identical in logic to Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig.safe_get_tenant_by_slug/1 (lib/letflow/routers/tenant_config.ex:193-203) -- same Identity.get_tenant_by_slug/1 call, same rescue clause, same INV-4 log-the-slug-not-the-exception behavior, differing only in the log message's module-name prefix string. This is not response-shape logic (which legitimately differs and should stay separate) -- it is a generic, security-sensitive (INV-4) lookup-and-rescue wrapper duplicated verbatim across two modules. This is the same class of defect docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Duplicating an Ecto.Query.fragment/1 SQL literal instead of sharing it via a module attribute' entry documents as FAIL/rework grounds: a real, low-risk, mechanical hoist is available (e.g. move this rescue-and-log behavior into Letflow.Identity itself, or a small shared helper both routers call), and leaving it duplicated creates the same silent-drift risk called out in that precedent -- a future INV-4 fix applied to one copy and not the other. This is narrow and does not implicate the two-module split, the response maps, the moduledocs, or the mount placement, all of which PASS.

issues.description: safe_get_tenant_by_slug/1 is duplicated verbatim (rescue clause, INV-4 log-the-slug-not-the-exception behavior, {:error, :lookup_failed} fallback) across the two router modules, differing only in a log-message prefix string. This is generic lookup/rescue plumbing, not response-shape logic, so hoisting it does not couple the two independently-audited response allowlists that the design's two-module split correctly protects.
issues.suggested_fix: Hoist the rescue-and-log wrapper into a single shared location both routers call -- e.g. fold it into Letflow.Identity.get_tenant_by_slug/1 itself so it never raises past the context boundary, or a small shared helper (e.g. Letflow.Identity.safe_get_tenant_by_slug/2 taking a caller-label for the log line) -- rather than two near-identical private functions in two router modules.
